# A composable other than the root's writing a var of its own named like one
# the root declares. In a test build android hoists the root's vars into a
# state class and renders each by name as `state.<name>`; the check that the
# var was the root's asked only that some component declared it, so the
# child's `count += 1` became `state.count += 1` in a composable with no
# `state`, and the build failed. An implicit-state wrapper's cells met the
# same when the page bound a var named `pending`
# (bubbletea_stateless_wrapper_built_instance_runs.txt).

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component counter ui.node {
    var count = 0
    ui.button #inc(text="{count}", @click { count += 1 })
}

component page ui.node {
    var count = 10
    var shown = true
    if shown {
        counter #child
    }
    ui.button #bump(text="{count}", @click { count += 1 })
}

func testEachCountIsItsOwn(t test.Test, c page) {
    t.assert(c.child != null)
    if c.child != null {
        c.child.inc.click()
        t.assert(c.child.count == 1)
        t.assert(c.count == 10)
        c.bump.click()
        t.assert(c.count == 11)
        t.assert(c.child.count == 1)
    }
}
